|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | intent | medium | The rewritten notice tells the model the block is unrecoverable, which the same PR's decision line denies: docs/changes/2026-11-08-unknown-content-tags.md:11 promises "an explicit whole-entry read (`history://<agent>/<entry-id>`, `user://<n>`) returns the entry as written", and crates/runtime/src/reclaim.rs:610 still tells a model read("history://{agent}/{entry}") for exactly this kind of kept content. So on load of the fixture's user message the model reads a row claiming nothing returns the block, while `user://<n>` (an ordinal it can count, no id needed) does return it as written: the one recovery route the feature keeps is now denied in-band, which is the failure mode 047-context-gathering records (a source the model is not pointed at does not exist). The author's own constraint (do not print a `<agent>/<entry-id>` placeholder the model cannot fill) is met by naming the read without an id, not by denying it. | `crates/types/src/message.rs:52` | Replace the last clause with a pointer that needs no id, e.g. "…the session file keeps it as written; a whole-entry read of the message (`user://<n>` for a user turn) returns it as written". |
| 2 | reuse | medium | (open since round 2) The Anthropic adapter maps an unread block to the notice itself, but `transform_messages` already does that mapping for every wire: `mark_unread` at crates/ai/src/transform.rs:55 rewrites `Content::Other` to a `Text` block holding `UNREAD_CONTENT`, and `convert_messages` only ever runs on `transform_messages` output (crates/ai/src/anthropic.rs:302 on `history`, and :362 on `transform_messages(...)` directly), so this arm can never fire. Two sources of truth for one rendering: a later change to the notice or to which blocks are readable lands here and has no effect, and the copies drift. | `crates/ai/src/anthropic.rs:184` | Delete the arm; `mark_unread` is the one place a block becomes its notice. |
| 3 | bloat | medium | (open since round 3) The Anthropic encoder renders an unread block as the notice itself, but nothing can reach that arm: `convert_messages` is only ever fed `transform_messages` output (anthropic.rs:282-302 and :362), and `mark_unread`/`unread_text` in transform.rs:47-59 already rewrite every `Content::Other` to a `Text` block holding `UNREAD_CONTENT` before encoding. That leaves a second source of truth for the one rendering: a later change to the notice, or to which blocks a provider may receive, lands here with no effect and the copies drift, while the conformance test, which counts notices rather than where they came from, stays green. | `crates/ai/src/anthropic.rs:184` | Fold the arm into the neighbouring no-op, `Content::Image { .. } \| Content::Other(_) => {}`, which keeps the match exhaustive and leaves `mark_unread` in transform.rs the one place a block becomes its notice; `openai` and `openai_responses` already get the notice that way through `join_text`. Drop the now-unused `UNREAD_CONTENT` import from the file's use list if nothing else there reads it. |
